processing_steps.method: vacuum arc melting with 4× remelting (ingot flipped before each remelt)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: M1 (Fe–8Mn–3Al-0.2C, Si-free) steel fabricated by vacuum arc melting; the melted ingot was remelted 4 times to ensure complete and uniform melting.
Homogenization of the as-cast samples (condition M1-HQ).

processing_steps.method: hot rolling followed by air cooling
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled at 1100 °C to reduce the thickness by 50 %, followed by air cooling (condition M1-HR); finish rolling temperature reached around 900 °C, causing formation of α-ferrite in M1.

processing_steps.method: intercritical annealing (IA) followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: IAT of 700 °C selected corresponding to ~11 % Mn in austenite for both steels; final condition M1-IA. Sample etched with 2 % Nital (2 ml nitric acid + 98 ml ethanol) for 10–15 s for microstructural analysis.

structures.overall_structure: Intercritically annealed M1-IA microstructure: mainly α-ferrite and austenite with a negligible amount of martensite. A wavy, banded/lamellar two-phase structure is observed in which austenite forms interconnected bands/stringers wrapping around large equiaxed ferrite grains. No δ-ferrite is present in M1.

phases_present.morphology: interpreted from EBSD phase map as elongated interconnected bands/stringers wrapping around large equiaxed ferrite grains

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Fig. 8b (M1, black): ~95 % of grains in the ~0.25–0.5 μm bin and ~5 % in the 0.5–1.0 μm bin; austenite grains both <0.5 μm and >0.5 μm present.

structures.overall_structure: Precursor M1-HR (hot-rolled) microstructure: polygonal α-ferrite plus lath-type martensitic-austenitic (α′ + γ) phase; XRD austenite fraction ~5 % (5.1 %).

interfaces.slip_behavior: Coarse austenite grains (γc, lower Mn and C) transform to martensite earlier, providing high work hardening at low strain; finer austenite grains (γf, higher Mn and C) undergo dislocation glide first and transform to martensite later, sustaining a constant work-hardening region over larger strains (TRIP with prior dislocation glide).
interfaces.phase_evolution: On heating the M1-HR microstructure (α-ferrite + α′+γ with ~5 % austenite) to the IAT, the unstable martensite first transforms into austenite and some α-ferrite also transforms towards the equilibrium ~50 % austenite. On cooling (water quenching) some austenite transforms back to martensite, leaving the observed ~45 % austenite. Mn (and C) partition from ferrite into austenite during IA; the finite 1 h anneal leaves transient Mn concentration gradients across the α/γ interface and locally Mn-enriched austenite.
interfaces.interface_notes: Local equilibrium at the α/γ interface during IA sets up Mn concentration gradients within α and γ that gradually diminish as the interface migrates into α; because the anneal is finite (1 h) some austenite remains locally Mn-enriched relative to equilibrium. The Mn concentration profile modelling is schematic (Fig. 9).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: dog-bone specimen: gauge length 2 mm, thickness 1 mm, width 1 mm (machined by wire-EDM)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile test on a Tinus-Olsen ST25 universal testing machine (UTM) with a 25 kN load cell.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve for M1-IA (red curve, Fig. 10a) peaks below 1000 MPa and extends to ~72 % strain (red square marker).

strain_hardening_rate.note: stage-II strain hardening rate value at point A (end of the gradual decline) for M1-IA; dσ/dε plotted vs true strain in Fig. 11a.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Austenite (γ) volume fraction measured on M1-IA before tensile testing (XRD via Rietveld-style direct comparison method) and after tensile fracture (EBSD phase map).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Product of strength and elongation (PSE): M1-IA = 61 GPa% vs M2-IA = 41 GPa%

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: After standard metallographic preparation and etching with 2 % Nital (2 ml nitric acid + 98 ml ethanol) for 10–15 s
characterization_methods.purpose: Obtain microstructural images of different samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used for microstructural imaging of the processing states (no numeric result reported).

characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), secondary electron (SE) mode
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: SE mode; M1-IA imaged at 20 µm, 5 µm, 3 µm and 2 µm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the phases and morphology of the M1-IA microstructure
characterization_methods.key_findings: M1-IA shows a wavy/lamellar multiphase structure with α-ferrite and α+γ regions; negligible martensite; no δ-ferrite in M1.

characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) phase mapping and Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) mapping
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD-OIM at the National Facility of Texture and OIM, IIT Bombay; post-processing software TSL OIM v8.5
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Phase maps with 5 µm scale bar; KAM colour bar Min 0 (blue) to Max 5 (red); measured before and after tensile testing
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure crystal orientation, phase distribution and deformation (KAM) of M1-IA
characterization_methods.key_findings: M1-IA consists of α-ferrite and austenite (orange-coded austenite forms interconnected bands/stringers); after tensile testing KAM increases markedly, and austenite fraction drops to 6.5 % (from 45 %), evidencing TRIP.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: PANalytical Empyrean diffractometer with Cu-Kα radiation (λ = 1.542 Å)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Diffraction angle (2θ) range 40–115°, step size 0.03°; austenite volume fraction from integrated intensities and R factors
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification and quantitative austenite fraction of M1-IA
characterization_methods.key_findings: M1-IA shows γ (fcc) and α (bcc) reflections with fγ = 45.6 % (reported as 45 %); confirms α-ferrite + austenite.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Tinus-Olsen ST25 universal testing machine (UTM) with 25 kN load cell
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; dog-bone specimens of gauge length 2 mm, thickness 1 mm, width 1 mm (wire-EDM machined)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure mechanical properties (strength, elongation) of M1-IA
characterization_methods.key_findings: M1-IA: UTS 867 ± 10 MPa, total elongation 71.8 ± 0.5 %, PSE 61 GPa%.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Fractured M1-IA tensile samples, 10 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Understand the fracture behaviour of the tensile-tested samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: M1-IA exhibits ductile fracture with fine dimple rupture; austenite absorbs strain energy via transformation to martensite forming fine dimples.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe–8Mn-0.2C system with systematic Al (0–4 %) addition; lower critical temperature taken as 600 °C; computes equilibrium phase fractions and austenite composition vs temperature
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted phases used to select alloy composition and the 700 °C IAT; predicted equilibrium austenite fraction at IAT (~50 % for M1) compared with the measured 45 % (observed lower than predicted).

analytical_models.model_name: Predicted equilibrium austenite fraction vs temperature
analytical_models.equation_role: Determine equilibrium phase fractions of M1 as a function of IAT and select the annealing temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Fig. 2a: M1 austenite fraction rises with temperature; at 700 °C it lies between the 40 and 50 % gridlines (~50 %).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Elemental concentrations taken from the austenite phase at hot-rolling / IAT temperatures in wt.%
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated Ms values predict transformation of austenite to martensite during cooling, consistent with observed martensite.

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute the martensite-start temperature of the steel from austenite composition
analytical_models.model_note: Equation: Ms(°C) = 539 - 423C - 30.4Mn - 7.5Si + 30Al; computed for M1 steel as 319 °C (HR).

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Uses calculated Ms temperature and annealing temperature (RT as T); computed as a function of IAT
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated retained austenite at RT for M1-IA (~16 %) is significantly lower than the observed ~45 %; discrepancy attributed to local microstructural heterogeneity (Mn segregation and finer austenite grains).

analytical_models.equation_role: Calculate the fraction of austenite retained at room temperature from the Ms temperature

parameters.name: calculated retained austenite fraction at RT (M1-IA)

analytical_models.model_note: Equation: (1 - f) = exp{-0.011[Ms - T]}. For M1-IA (IAT = 700 °C) retained fraction computed ~16 %.

computational_details.simulation_method: Exponential decay fitting of retained-austenite fraction with true strain (TRIP kinetics)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: A = austenite fraction before tensile test (45.6 % for M1-IA); fitted to the fraction after fracture at maximum strain
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Fit parameter B = 3.6 for M1; lower B indicates higher mechanical stability / slower TRIP for M1 than M2 (B = 3.8).

analytical_models.model_name: Austenite transformation kinetics fγ = A × e^(-Bε)
analytical_models.equation_role: Model the transformation of retained austenite to martensite as a function of true strain and quantify mechanical stability

parameters.name: A (austenite fraction before tensile test, M1)

unmapped_findings: Stacking fault energy (SFE) of M1 (and M2) steel is below 18 mJ/m², a critical value below which the alloy is expected to show the TRIP effect; transformation of austenite to martensite is expected during deformation, resulting in improved elongation.

The austenite fraction of M1-IA before tensile testing is 45 % (XRD 45.6 %) and after tensile fracture it drops to 6.5 % (EBSD), a significant reduction demonstrating transformation of austenite to martensite during tensile deformation (TRIP effect).

The observed M1-IA austenite fraction (~45 %) is significantly higher than the fraction calculated from the Koistinen-Marburger model based on the equilibrium Mn content (~11 %, calculated ~16 %); this discrepancy is attributed to local microstructural heterogeneity — Mn segregation/local enrichment in austenite grains and the presence of a high fraction of fine austenite grains (<0.5 μm) with higher C, which raise austenite stability.
M1 steel forms α-ferrite (rather than δ-ferrite) during hot rolling because the finish rolling temperature reaches around 900 °C; no δ-ferrite is present in the M1-IA sample (unlike M2).
The M1-HR (precursor) sample shows UTS of 1712 ± 10 MPa and total elongation of 14.8 ± 0.5 % with a brittle cleavage fracture (flat facets), contrasting with the ductile M1-IA sample.
